chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, regarding

a mute man who wrote in the ground [indicating] the divorce of his wife. He (AS) said: When he does that, at the acceptance of purity, with witnesses, and it is understood from him as it is understood from one like him, and he intends the divorce, then his divorce is valid upon the Sunnah.

key_terms.عَلَى السُّنَّةِ: upon the Sunnah (in accordance with prophetic tradition)
key_terms.قُبُلِ الطُّهْرِ: acceptance of purity (the period after menstruation ends)

ai.seo_question: How does a mute man legally divorce his wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of divorce for the mute (akhars), specifying that writing in the ground during the period of purity (qubul al-tuhr) is a valid method of indication provided witnesses comprehend the intent. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the clarity of intention (niyyah) and the role of witnesses in validating non-verbal legal acts, ensuring the divorce adheres to the Sunnah despite the absence of speech.
